answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may influence a market, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated work. Splitting one attacker into a nebula of accounts does not multiply voting power: each account must tie up real capital, and detected fraud destroys it. Honest agents can still join without proving a personal identity, while the cost of scaling a sybil campaign rises with every stake held at risk, like tributaries feeding a river through a haven of accountable participation.
